messages.body_plain:
Our take on standard errors is different from Abadie and Imbens.  It's
described in this paper: http://imai.princeton.edu/research/preprocess.html

Kosuke Imai
Department of Politics
Princeton University
http://imai.princeton.edu

matthieu.stigler-Re5JQEeQqe8AvxtiuMwx3w at public.gmane.org> wrote:

> Besides these issues, I was wondering what exactly is the approach you
> suggest to estimate the ATE/ATT in this code? It looks to me it is based on
> simulating/bootstrapping the counterfactuals? But my understanding was that
> the bootstrap was not consistent for matching estimates, as shown by Abadie
> and Imbens (2008)?
>
> Also, how does this approach compare to the methods implemented in the
> Matching package, function Match, that implements bias correction and
> adjusted standard errors? Is there anyway to use the output of MatchIt to
> be estimated with the Match function instead of the simulation approach in
> Zelig?
>
> Thanks!
>
> Matthieu

z <- m/sqrt(a/2)
the results match with matchit...

messages.body_plain:
Hi Bonitta,
This page explains how the standardized mean difference is calculated in matchit:

http://r.iq.harvard.edu/docs/matchit/2.4-20/Output_Values2.html

Basically it uses weighted means in the numerator, using the weights generated by full matching.

Liz

messages.subject: SD Control vs SD Treated in summary.matchit with standardize = TRUE
messages.subject_clean: SD Control vs SD Treated in summary.matchit with standardize = TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Dear MatchIt Mailing List,

when I calculated some summary statistics to compare means before and after
matching, I used the standardized = TRUE option to obtain standardized mean
differences. However, to my surprise, the output shows that the standard
deviation in the control group is used for standardization (where I felt
the SD of the treatment group was more appropriate but I can live with
that). You can produce the output I am referring to via:

summary(matchit(formula = treat~re74+re75+ black+hispan+educ+age, data =
lalonde), standardized = TRUE)

As I was unsure which SD was used to standardize, I dug in the code and
noticed, that in the MatchIt:::qoi function the SD is actually calculated
from the treatment group, i.e. I am almost sure that in the code of qoi,
the SD of the treated is calculated.

I am using a very recently built version of Matchit from CRAN but the
underlying code seems not to have been updated since 2013. Has this been
addressed/fixed in the meantime?

With kind wishes,
   Philipp Doebler

messages.subject_clean: SD Control vs SD Treated in summary.matchit with standardize = TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Could this be more of a reporting than a calculation issue? In other words, if the treatment group SD is used in standardization, then it would follow that the treatment SD on the standardized outcome would be 1.0. So the SD of the control group is reported since it was not used to standardize the variable and could be a value other than 1.0.

 

Barth

 

 

From: matchit-bounces-boHuZhbfW+Y6DHxCPSz5rL5+avTOL6Rl at public.gmane.org [mailto:matchit-bounces-boHuZhbfW+Y6DHxCPSz5rL5+avTOL6Rl at public.gmane.org] On Behalf Of Philipp Doebler
Sent: Tuesday, May 19, 2015 1:05 PM
To: matchit-boHuZhbfW+Y6DHxCPSz5rL5+avTOL6Rl at public.gmane.org
Subject: [matchit] SD Control vs SD Treated in summary.matchit with standardize = TRUE

 

Dear MatchIt Mailing List,


when I calculated some summary statistics to compare means before and after matching, I used the standardized = TRUE option to obtain standardized mean differences. However, to my surprise, the output shows that the standard deviation in the control group is used for standardization (where I felt the SD of the treatment group was more appropriate but I can live with that). You can produce the output I am referring to via:

summary(matchit(formula = treat~re74+re75+ black+hispan+educ+age, data = lalonde), standardized = TRUE)

As I was unsure which SD was used to standardize, I dug in the code and noticed, that in the MatchIt:::qoi function the SD is actually calculated from the treatment group, i.e. I am almost sure that in the code of qoi, the SD of the treated is calculated.

I am using a very recently built version of Matchit from CRAN but the underlying code seems not to have been updated since 2013. Has this been addressed/fixed in the meantime?

With kind wishes,
   Philipp Doebler

messages.body_plain:
Dear Philipp,

  This is one way of standardizing the mean difference.  The key here is
that you don't want the standard deviation to change before and after
matching.  You could have chosen the standard deviation from the treatment
group, but I don't see a strong theoretical reason to prefer one over
another.

Best,
Kosuke

Kosuke Imai
Department of Politics
Princeton University
http://imai.princeton.edu
